# Conformance matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_conformance.py from docs/conformance.json: do not edit. -->

What each CDDL construct, control operator and CBOR item does in each layer of the library, and how that is tested. Every claim is checked by `tests/test_conformance.py`, which runs the examples in [docs/conformance.json](conformance.json) against the code, so this page cannot describe behaviour the code does not have. See [CDDL_SUPPORT.md](CDDL_SUPPORT.md) for how each supported construct behaves.

| Mark | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| ✅ | supported: accepted, resolved and enforced; examples and tests cover it |
| 🟡 | partial: works for some uses; the notes say which |
| ❌ | unsupported: the layer does not do it (an operator that is parsed but not enforced accepts any value) |
| – | not applicable to this layer |
| ⛔ | out of scope |

Layers: the **parser** reads the syntax into the typed **AST**; the **resolver** checks names, kinds and controls and reports `SchemaError`s; the **validator** checks data; **EDN** is the annotated diagnostic output; **JSON** is the typed JSON bridge.

## Summary

| Area | ✅ supported | 🟡 partial | ❌ unsupported | Total |
|------|-------------:|-----------:|---------------:|------:|
| CDDL syntax and semantics | 28 | 0 | 0 | 28 |
| Control operators | 34 | 0 | 0 | 34 |
| Prelude types (RFC 8610 Appendix D) | 15 | 0 | 0 | 15 |
| CBOR data model (RFC 8949) | 11 | 0 | 0 | 11 |

## CDDL syntax and semantics

Constructs of the RFC 8610 grammar (as updated by RFC 9682), the modules draft, and the schema checks done before any data is seen.

| Construct | Spec | Status | Parser | AST | Resolver | Validator | EDN | Notes | Tests |
|---|---|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|---|---|
| Type rules `name = type` | RFC 8610 §2.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The first rule is the default root; `--type` / `root_type` selects another. | `test_cddl_parser.py`, `test_resolve.py`, `test_public_api.py` |
| Type extension `name /= type` | RFC 8610 §2.2.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Adds alternatives to a type or a socket. | `test_type_choices.py`, `test_resolve.py` |
| Group extension `name //= group` | RFC 8610 §2.2.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Adds a group choice alternative; sockets (`$$name`) are extended the same way. | `test_group_composition.py`, `test_resolve.py` |
| Type choice `a / b` | RFC 8610 §2.2.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Resolved by checking every alternative; ambiguity is reported with `unique_choices` (#74). | `test_type_choices.py`, `test_choice_resolution.py` |
| Group choice `(a // b)` | RFC 8610 §2.2.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | In maps (including products of several choices, up to 1024 combinations) and in arrays. A choice repeated in a map (`{+ g}`, `{* $$socket}`) lets each repetition take any alternative, so entries of several can be mixed (#201). | `test_group_composition.py`, `test_array_matching.py`, `test_map_repetition.py` |
| Occurrence indicators `?` `*` `+` `n*m` | RFC 8610 §3.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | On array entries (also entries that are sockets, #223), map members, groups and wildcard members (bounds and the default of exactly one are enforced, #151). [#223](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/223) | `test_array_length.py`, `test_group_composition.py`, `test_array_matching.py`, `test_socket_occurrences.py` |
| Maps `{ ... }` | RFC 8610 §3.5 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Members with bareword, text, integer (also negative), byte-string, bool, float and type keys; maps are closed unless a wildcard member allows more. A `null` (or `nil`) key written with `=>` is a required member like any other; `null: T` is the text key `"null"`. | `test_map_key_types.py`, `test_legacy_tables.py`, `test_group_composition.py` |
| Cuts `^` (`"a" ^=> T`) | RFC 8610 §3.5.4 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | A cut (`^=>`, and `:`) stops later wildcard members from claiming the key. `K => T` has no cut: when its value is not a `T`, a later wildcard may take the entry (#202). | `test_group_composition.py`, `test_map_repetition.py` |
| Arrays `[ ... ]` | RFC 8610 §3.4 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Entries are matched in order with backtracking, so an optional entry before another is fine (#135); lengths are checked (#133). | `test_array_matching.py`, `test_array_length.py` |
| Groups, group references and inline groups | RFC 8610 §3.3 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | In maps and arrays, with occurrences, choices, sockets, recursion (also through arrays, #138) and generics (#72). | `test_group_composition.py`, `test_array_matching.py` |
| Unwrap `~name` | RFC 8610 §3.7 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Splices the entries of a map or array into a map or array, and unwraps a tag as a type (#158). A map or array in a place that needs a type is a group, not a type, and matches nothing. | `test_group_composition.py`, `test_type_choices.py` |
| Choices from groups `&(...)` and `&name` | RFC 8610 §2.2.2.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The choice of the values of a group's entries. | `test_type_choices.py` |
| Generic rules `name<T> = ...` | RFC 8610 §3.9 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Instantiated where used (also in control arguments, #127); recursive generics terminate. | `test_resolve.py`, `test_legacy_tables.py`, `test_and_within.py` |
| Type and group sockets `$name`, `$$name` | RFC 8610 §3.9 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | An empty socket matches nothing; extensions (`/=`, `//=`) from the schema and its modules are merged. In an array a socket takes its occurrence like any other entry: a type socket is one element and a group socket one of its groups (#223). [#223](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/223) | `test_type_choices.py`, `test_group_composition.py`, `test_socket_occurrences.py` |
| Recursive rules | RFC 8610 §2.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Self-referencing types, groups and generics; a rule defined only in terms of itself (`a = b`, `b = a`) is a schema error. | `test_array_matching.py`, `test_resolve.py` |
| Identifiers with `-`, `_`, `.`, `$` and `@` | RFC 8610 §3.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Includes dotted names such as `a.b`. | `test_cddl_parser.py` |
| Comments, whitespace and trailing commas | RFC 8610 §3.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | – | – | Syntax only: there is no data to reject. `0: tstr ; name` comments name fields in EDN (deprecation planned, #108). [#108](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/108) | `test_cddl_parser.py`, `test_cddl_parser.py` |
| Integer literals (decimal, `0x`, `0b`) | RFC 8610 §3.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Matched exactly; a float does not match an integer literal. | `test_literal_types.py` |
| Float literals (decimal, exponent, hexadecimal) | RFC 8610 §3.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Matched exactly; the integer 1 does not match 1.0. | `test_literal_types.py` |
| Text literals with escapes | RFC 8610 §3.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |  | `test_literal_types.py` |
| Byte-string literals (`h'..'`, `b64'..'`, `'text'`) | RFC 8610 §3.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |  | `test_literal_types.py` |
| Ranges `a..b`, `a...b` | RFC 8610 §3.8.3 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Integer and float bounds, inclusive and exclusive; bounds of different kinds, or an empty range, are schema errors (#71). | `test_ranges.py` |
| Tags `#6.n(type)` | RFC 8610 §3.6 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Tag number and content are checked; nesting works. Data holds a tag as a `CBORTag`. | `test_tag_validation.py` |
| Tag number given as a type `#6.<type>(t)` | RFC 9682 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Checked as the root rule, a map field, an array element and a choice alternative: the item must be a tag whose number matches `<type>` (`#6.<uint .le 10>(t)`, `#6.<1 / 2>(t)`) and whose content matches `t`. `#6(t)` accepts any tag. A bignum the decoder returns as an integer counts as tag 2 or 3. | `test_item_refs.py`, `test_cddl_parser.py` |
| Major types `#M`, `#M.N`, `#` | RFC 8610 §3.6 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | `#M` matches the major type, `#M.N` the additional information of the head (the value or length below 24, the width of its argument for 24-27, 31 for an indefinite length; a float written as a double is `#7.27`), `#7.20`-`#7.23` false, true, null and undefined, other `#7.N` a simple value, `#6` any tag, `#6.N` a tag numbered N (the number is the tag number, not additional information), and `#` any item; as the root rule, field, element or choice alternative. Data given as Python values is taken to be written the preferred way. | `test_item_refs.py`, `test_cbor_items_extended.py`, `test_cddl_parser.py` |
| Modules `;# import X as P`, `;# include X` | draft-ietf-cbor-cddl-modules | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Draft comment syntax. Modules come from `modules=` / `--module` or a search path; one that is not found keeps its names unchecked and warns (#121), or is a schema error at its directive with `strict_modules=True` / `--strict-modules` (#229). No RFC modules are bundled. | `test_modules.py` |
| Root rules that are not maps or arrays | RFC 8610 §2.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Primitives with controls, choices, literals and tags work as the root type (#94). | `test_type_choices.py`, `test_public_api.py` |
| Name resolution and schema errors | RFC 8610 §2 | ✅ | – | – | ✅ | – | – | Undefined names (with suggestions), duplicate definitions, wrong generic argument counts, unknown controls and misapplied controls are `SchemaError`s with a position (#70). | `test_resolve.py`, `test_cddl_parser.py` |

## Control operators

Every operator the resolver knows (RFC 8610, RFC 9165, RFC 9741). An operator the validator does not enforce still parses and resolves, and accepts any value.

| Construct | Spec | Status | Parser | AST | Resolver | Validator | EDN | Notes | Tests |
|---|---|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|---|---|
| `.size` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Integers (number of bytes), byte and text strings (bytes of UTF-8), with a number or a range argument (#67). | `test_size_control.py` |
| `.bits` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Only the bit positions the argument names may be set, for a `uint` and a `bstr` (the first byte is least significant: bit 8 is the lowest bit of the second byte). The argument is a uint, a range, a choice of them, or a rule or `&(...)` that is. Anything else is a schema error; the message names the stray bit. | `test_bits_regexp.py` |
| `.regexp` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The pattern is an XSD regular expression, as RFC 8610 says, matched by an NFA in time linear in the text (#185): the whole text must match, `^` and `$` are ordinary characters, `\d`, `\w`, `\s`, `\i`, `\c`, `\p{...}` and `\P{...}` follow XSD, and a class can subtract another (`[a-z-[aeiou]]`). Unicode categories come from the running Python and every Unicode block is known (`\p{IsGreek}`, `\p{IsBraillePatterns}`; #231). A pattern XSD does not have (lazy quantifier, `(?:`, back reference) or an unknown category or block is a schema error naming it. A pattern needing more than 50 000 NFA states is a schema error; a match over 10 million steps is refused. | `test_bits_regexp.py`, `test_cbor_control_args.py` |
| `.cbor` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The byte string must hold one CBOR item matching the argument (named types, structures and generic instances, #127); errors inside it are offset-mapped to the outer bytes. | `test_cbor_control_args.py`, `test_cbor_control_args.py` |
| `.cborseq` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The byte string must hold a CBOR sequence (RFC 8742) whose items, taken as an array, match the argument, which must be an array type: `bstr .cborseq [* uint]` takes any number of uints, including none. A truncated or malformed item is reported with its number and offset. The error is reported at the byte string, as for `.cbor`. | `test_cborseq.py` |
| `.within` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The data must match the target and the argument, for any target: a primitive, a choice, a rule, a tag, a map or an array (`non-empty<M>` is the generic case, #120). `.within` is checked as `.and`, since only values are validated. [#120](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/120) | `test_set_controls.py`, `test_and_within.py` |
| `.and` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The data must match the target and the argument, for any target: a primitive, a choice, a rule, a tag, a map or an array (`non-empty<M>` is the generic case, #120). `.within` is checked as `.and`, since only values are validated. [#120](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/120) | `test_set_controls.py`, `test_and_within.py` |
| `.lt` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Numbers (less than the argument); integers and floats. | `test_cbor_control_args.py`, `test_size_control.py` |
| `.le` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Numbers (at most the argument); integers and floats. | `test_cbor_control_args.py`, `test_size_control.py` |
| `.gt` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Numbers (greater than the argument); integers and floats. | `test_cbor_control_args.py`, `test_size_control.py` |
| `.ge` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Numbers (at least the argument); integers and floats. | `test_cbor_control_args.py`, `test_size_control.py` |
| `.eq` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The data equals the argument, which must be one value: a literal, `true`, `false`, `null`, `undefined` or a rule that is one. Any other argument is a schema error. | `test_set_controls.py` |
| `.ne` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The data differs from the argument, which must be one value, as for `.eq`. | `test_set_controls.py` |
| `.default` | RFC 8610 §3.8 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Advisory: the data must match the base type; the default value itself is not applied. | `test_cbor_control_args.py` |
| `.plus` | RFC 9165 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Both operands must be numbers (literals, rules that are literals, ranges or choices of them); the result is a number of the type of the target (a float target gives a float, an integer target the floor of the sum). A result with several values, or a range, is a type to match; one value is also a fixed map key (`(BASE .plus 1) => int`). Operands that are not literals (`uint .plus 1`) are a schema error. | `test_computed_literals.py` |
| `.cat` | RFC 9165 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The result has the type of the target: bytes of both operands are joined, and a text result must be valid UTF-8. Operands that are not string literals (`tstr .cat "a"`) are a schema error. | `test_computed_literals.py` |
| `.det` | RFC 9165 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Like `.cat`, after each operand is dedented: the smallest number of leading spaces on its non-blank lines is removed from every line (RFC 9165 section 2.3). | `test_computed_literals.py` |
| `.abnf` | RFC 9165 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The string must be in the language of the ABNF text of the argument (RFC 5234 with RFC 7405; one element, then the rules, a single linefeed as newline; all rules must be in the text). Text is read as code points; a byte string as UTF-8. Left recursion and ambiguity are handled; a match that needs more than 2 million steps is rejected. Prose and undefined rules are schema errors. | `test_abnf.py`, `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.abnfb` | RFC 9165 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Like `.abnf`, with the ABNF read over the bytes of the string (a text string as UTF-8). | `test_abnf.py`, `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.feature` | RFC 9165 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | RFC 9165 section 4. The controller is a feature name or an array of the name and a detail (a schema error otherwise). By default every feature is enabled and the data must match the base type. Given `features` (`--feature NAME`, `--no-features`), only the named features are enabled. `T .feature F` then matches while F is enabled; while it is not, the target does not match, the message names F, and a choice falls through to its other alternatives. The RFC leaves that behaviour to the tool. `ValidationResult.features_used` lists the features of the parts that matched. A generic parameter as the controller is accepted (#243). [#243](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/243) | `test_feature_control.py`, `test_resolve.py` |
| `.b64u` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is base64url without padding (RFC 4648 section 5) and its bytes match the argument; no other alphabet, no padding, no blank space, and no non-zero bits after the last character. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.b64c` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is classic base64 with padding (RFC 4648 section 4) and its bytes match the argument; no non-zero bits after the last character. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.b64u-sloppy` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Like `.b64u`, but bits after the last character may be non-zero. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.b64c-sloppy` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Like `.b64c`, but bits after the last character may be non-zero. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.b45` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is base45 (RFC 9285) and its bytes match the argument. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.b32` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is base32 without padding (RFC 4648 section 6, upper case) and its bytes match the argument. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.h32` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is base32 with the extended hex alphabet and no padding (RFC 4648 section 7, upper case) and its bytes match the argument. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.hex` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is hexadecimal in either case (RFC 4648 section 8) and its bytes match the argument; no blank space. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.hexlc` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Like `.hex`, in lower case only. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.hexuc` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Like `.hex`, in upper case only. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.base10` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is a decimal integer without leading zeros (`0\|-?[1-9][0-9]*`) and its value matches the argument. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.printf` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is what C `printf` writes for the format (the first element of the argument array) and data items that match the other elements, which may be types. Conversions `d i u o x X e E f F g G a A c s` with flags, width and precision (a `*` takes the next data item, as in C: `["%*d", 5, uint]`, #241); length modifiers, `p` and `n` are schema errors. The text is taken apart by the format and each conversion read back and written again, so only exact output matches. Where a format can be split in several ways (adjacent `%s`, or a literal that can also be inside a `%s`), every split is tried and the text is valid if one of them gives items of the right types, within a budget of 200,000 steps. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.json` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The text is one JSON value (RFC 8259: no `NaN`, no repeated member names) and its conversion to the CBOR data model (RFC 8949 section 6.2) matches the argument. | `test_text_controls.py` |
| `.join` | RFC 9741 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The string is the concatenation of strings that match the elements of the argument array, written out and each once: literal elements are markers, the others take what is between them and must fit their type (as text or as bytes). The result is the kind of string of the first element. A string that can be split in too many ways (adjacent variable elements) is rejected after 20000 tries. | `test_text_controls.py` |

## Prelude types (RFC 8610 Appendix D)

One row per group of related names.

| Construct | Spec | Status | Parser | AST | Resolver | Validator | EDN | Notes | Tests |
|---|---|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|---|---|
| `any` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |  | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `bool`, `true`, `false` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Integers 0 and 1 do not match. | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `nil`, `null` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |  | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `undefined` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Matches the CBOR `undefined` item and nothing else (not `null`); `any` and `#` match it too. | `test_prelude_types.py`, `test_cbor_items_extended.py` |
| `uint`, `nint`, `int` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Booleans do not match; `int` is the 64-bit range, bignums are `biguint`/`bignint`. | `test_prelude_types.py`, `test_cbor_cddl_analyzer.py` |
| `biguint`, `bignint`, `bigint`, `integer`, `unsigned` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Tags 2 and 3 (bignums). | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `bstr`, `bytes` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |  | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `tstr`, `text` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |  | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `float16`, `float32`, `float64`, `float`, `float16-32`, `float32-64` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | `float16`, `float32` and `float64` follow the encoding of data decoded from bytes (`float16` rejects a float written as a double). A float given as a Python value has no encoding and matches a width it can be written in without loss (`1.5` is `float16`, `1.1` is only `float64`). `float` and the choices accept every float width they name; integers never match. | `test_prelude_types.py`, `test_cbor_items_extended.py` |
| `number` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | `int / float`. | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `tdate`, `time` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | `tdate` is tag 0 around an RFC 3339 date-time: the calendar must be valid (no 2021-02-29, no month 13), the time `hh:mm:ss` valid, the offset `Z` or `+hh:mm`. Second 60 is accepted only as 23:59:60 UTC at the end of March, June, September or December. `time` is tag 1 around a number. | `test_prelude_types.py`, `test_tag_content.py` |
| `decfrac`, `bigfloat` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Tags 4 and 5 holding `[exponent, mantissa]`. | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `eb64url`, `eb64legacy`, `eb16`, `cbor-any` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | Tag numbers 21, 22, 23 and 55799. | `test_prelude_types.py` |
| `encoded-cbor`, `uri`, `b64url`, `b64legacy`, `regexp` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The tag number, the type of the content (a byte string under tags 2, 3 and 24, text under 0 and 32 to 36, even under `#6.2(any)`; #234) and what the content means: `encoded-cbor` is one well-formed CBOR item, `uri` an RFC 3986 URI reference, `b64url` base64url text without padding, `b64legacy` base64 text with padding; for both the unused bits of the last character are 0. `regexp` is checked as a Python `re` pattern (with `(?<name>...)` and `\k<name>` accepted), which approximates PCRE and ECMA-262 but does not accept every construct of either. | `test_prelude_types.py`, `test_tag_content.py` |
| `mime-message` | RFC 8610 Appendix D | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – | The tag number is checked, and the text must be a MIME message (RFC 5322, RFC 2045, RFC 2046): header fields (folding allowed), then optionally an empty line and a body; `MIME-Version`, `Content-Type` and `Content-Transfer-Encoding` well formed and not repeated; a `multipart` body needs a valid boundary, its delimiters, and every part checked the same way (nested up to 10 levels). Lines may end in CRLF or LF and headers may hold UTF-8. The body is not decoded (`base64`, `quoted-printable`, `message/rfc822`). [#187](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/187) | `test_mime_message.py`, `test_prelude_types.py`, `test_tag_content.py` |

## CBOR data model (RFC 8949)

What the decoder, encoder, validator, EDN output and typed JSON bridge do with each kind of item.

| Construct | Spec | Status | Decoder | Encoder | Validator | EDN | JSON | Notes | Tests |
|---|---|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|---|---|
| Integers (major types 0 and 1, up to 64 bits) | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Non-shortest encodings are accepted by `loads()` (`1800` is 0); the optional deterministic check is #95. [#95](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/95) | `test_rfc8949_conformance.py`, `test_strict_decoding.py` |
| Byte and text strings (definite length) | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Text strings must be valid UTF-8. | `test_rfc8949_conformance.py`, `test_strict_decoding.py` |
| Arrays and maps (definite length) | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Duplicate map keys are rejected (#65); non-string keys keep their type (#88). [#92](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/92) | `test_rfc8949_conformance.py`, `test_map_key_types.py`, `test_strict_decoding.py` |
| `false`, `true`, `null` | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |  | `test_rfc8949_conformance.py` |
| Floats (half, single, double) | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | All three widths decode to a Python float, and `keep_encoding=True` (the validator's decoding) records the width so `float16`, `float32` and `float64` check it. The encoder writes a float in the shortest width that keeps the value (RFC 8949 §4.1) in both modes; `float_width(value, bits)` fixes the width of one value, and a float decoded with `keep_encoding=True` is written in the width it had (#96). [#96](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/96) | `test_deterministic_encoding.py`, `test_float_serialization.py`, `test_rfc8949_conformance.py` |
| Tags (major type 6) | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Tags decode to `CBORTag(number, value)` and `CBORTag` encodes as a tag. A `(number, value)` tuple is not a tag: the encoder and the typed JSON conversion raise `TypeError` for one. Bignums (2, 3) outside the 64-bit range decode to Python ints in values. | `test_cbor_tag.py`, `test_tag_validation.py`, `test_rfc8949_conformance.py` |
| Indefinite-length strings, arrays and maps | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Decoded to the same Python values as definite-length items, with chunks joined; the encoder and typed JSON write them back definite-length. A break with nothing to end, a missing break, a chunk of the wrong type, a map that ends after a key, and an indefinite integer or tag are rejected. `#4.31` and `#5.31` (also `#2.31`, `#3.31`) match them when the data is decoded from bytes. | `test_cbor_items_extended.py` |
| `undefined` and the other simple values | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | `undefined` decodes to `UNDEFINED` and the other simple values (0-19, 32-255) to `CBORSimple(n)`; they encode back, keep their type as map keys, and appear in typed JSON as `{"$cbor": "undefined"}` and `{"$cbor": "simple", "$value": n}` (untyped: `null` and the number). The two-byte form below 32 and the reserved informations 28-30 are not well-formed. | `test_cbor_items_extended.py` |
| One complete item per input | RFC 8949 | ✅ | ✅ | – | – | – | – | `loads()` rejects empty, truncated and trailing data; a sequence API is #77. [#77](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/77) | `test_strict_decoding.py` |
| Core deterministic encoding (§4.2.1) | RFC 8949 | ✅ | – | ✅ | – | – | – | Shortest integers and floats, map keys sorted by encoded bytes, definite lengths. The optional §4.2.2 reduction of integral floats is not applied. | `test_deterministic_encoding.py`, `test_canonical_and_json.py` |
| Typed JSON bridge | project format | ✅ | – | – | – | – | ✅ | `typed=True` keeps byte strings, tags and non-string keys so the JSON converts back to the same CBOR; hardening of the annotations is #79. [#79](https://github.com/sahebbiswas/cddl_verifier/issues/79) | `test_canonical_and_json.py`, `test_json_map_keys.py` |

## Out of scope

| Item | Why |
|------|-----|
| Reading EDN text | The library writes annotated EDN from CBOR; it does not parse EDN into CBOR. |
| Signatures, MACs and cryptographic checks (COSE, CoRIM, EAT) | Validation is structural: the library checks the shape of the data, not what the data attests. |
| Generating sample data from a schema | Schemas are used to validate and annotate data that already exists. |
| CDDL outside RFC 8610, RFC 9165, RFC 9682, RFC 9741 and the modules draft comment syntax | Unknown control operators are schema errors; a second control on one type (`uint .ge 0 .le 150`, accepted before #113) is a syntax error that names the parenthesized spelling; nothing else non-standard is accepted. |

## Updating

Edit [conformance.json](conformance.json), then run `python scripts/render_conformance.py` to rewrite this page. A change that adds a construct, enforces a control, or fixes a gap needs its row in the same pull request:

- `status` is `supported`, `partial`, `unsupported` or `out-of-scope`; `layers` gives each layer `supported`, `partial`, `unsupported` or `n/a`. A row that is not supported names the issue that tracks it.
- `tests` lists the test files that cover the row (they must exist).
- `probes` are run by the test. Each has a `schema` (and optionally a `root` or `modules`) and lists of data: `valid` must be accepted, `invalid` rejected. `accepted_but_invalid` and `rejected_but_valid` record a known gap, and the test fails when the code stops behaving that way, so a fix cannot leave the row behind. Data is JSON, with `{"$bytes": hex}`, `{"$tag": n, "$value": v}`, `{"$map": [[k, v], ...]}`, `{"$float": "nan"}`, `{"$undefined": true}` and `{"$simple": n}` for what JSON cannot write.
- `schema_errors` are schemas that must raise `SchemaError`.
- `cbor` items (CBOR rows) give the hex input, whether it decodes, and whether it round-trips through the encoder, the canonical encoder and typed JSON.
- New controls and prelude names need a row (`covers` lists the prelude names a row stands for): the test compares them with what the resolver and prelude define.
